questions.question: What is the primary responsibility of the manufacturing and production function in any organization?
options: B) Producing the firm's goods and services
questions.answer: B) Producing the firm's goods and services
questions.explanation: The manufacturing and production function in any organization is responsible for actually producing the firm's goods and services.

questions.question: A company produces goods to create an inventory of finished products that are stored in a warehouse and available for sales. This strategy is also known as a:
questions.answer: C) Push process
questions.explanation: Make-to-stock production process, where goods are produced to create or increase inventory available for sales, is also known as a push process.

questions.question: Which manufacturing strategy minimizes or eliminates the question of holding finished goods inventory?
questions.answer: C) Make-to-order
questions.explanation: Make-to-order process occurs when production is generated by a specific customer order, and hence the question of holding finished goods inventory is minimized or eliminated.

questions.question: In a simplified manufacturing process, what immediately follows the customer placing an order and the warehouse checking for sufficient stock, if the stock is insufficient or a specific order is placed?
options: B) Generating a material withdrawal slip
questions.answer: C) Issuing a planned order
questions.explanation: When the customer places an order, the first thing checked is stock. If insufficient inventory or a specific order for out-of-stock goods, the warehouse department issues a planned order.

questions.question: What is the primary goal of production or manufacturing management?
options: B) To maximize production of goods and services at the highest cost
C) To optimally deploy human resources, machines, and materials to maximize production at the least cost
D) To solely focus on marketing finished products
questions.answer: C) To optimally deploy human resources, machines, and materials to maximize production at the least cost
questions.explanation: The goal of production or manufacturing management is to optimally deploy human resources, machines and materials to maximize production of goods and services by the organization, preferably at the least cost.

questions.question: Information regarding the location of new production facilities and the design of new products (using CAD) falls under which category of information required for manufacturing management?
questions.answer: C) Strategic information
questions.explanation: Examples of strategic information include location of new production facilities and design of new products.

questions.question: Identifying and controlling areas of high cost, such as minimizing work-in-progress inventories, is an example of what type of information requirement for a manufacturing function?
questions.answer: B) Tactical
questions.explanation: Identification and control of areas of high cost, for example, how to minimize work in progress inventories, are examples of tactical information required for a manufacturing function.

questions.question: Monitoring up-to-date production information, detecting likely shortages, and generating early warnings are examples of what type of information required for manufacturing management?
questions.answer: C) Operational information
questions.explanation: Operational information comprises monitoring up to date production information by examining assemblies, detecting likely shortages and generating early warning.

questions.question: Which subsystem of information systems for manufacturing management is responsible for maintaining data on all production-related activities, generating sales forecasts, and managing the bill of material?
questions.answer: C) Production Planning Subsystem
questions.explanation: The production planning subsystem maintains data on all production related activities, generates sales forecasts and plans, and facilitates maintenance of the bill of material.

questions.question: For a company that manufactures personal computers, the demand for the finished personal computers themselves is considered an:
questions.answer: C) Independent demand item
questions.explanation: Independent demand items are those items for which the demand does not depend on anything else. For example, the number of identical personal computers a computer manufacturer will sell, their demand is basically independent demand.

questions.question: Screws and bolts used in the assembly of three different types of chairs by a company are examples of:
questions.answer: C) Dependent demand items
questions.explanation: The demand for screws and bolts depends on the total demand for all three types of chairs and their shipment schedules, making them interdependent or dependent demand items.

questions.question: What is the primary focus of Materials Requirement Planning (MRP)?
options: C) Planning process that integrates production, purchasing, and inventory management of interdependent items
questions.answer: C) Planning process that integrates production, purchasing, and inventory management of interdependent items
questions.explanation: The planning process that integrates production, purchasing and inventory management of interdependent items is the primary focus of materials requirement planning.

questions.question: One of the main functions of an MRP system is to:
options: A) Determine customer preferences for new products
B) Monitor stocks and determine which material managers need, in what quantity, at what point of time
C) Manage employee payroll and benefits
questions.answer: B) Monitor stocks and determine which material managers need, in what quantity, at what point of time
questions.explanation: The main functions of a material requirement planning process are to monitor stocks and to determine which material the managers need in what quantity, at what point of time.

questions.question: In MRP, what does "pipeline stock" refer to?
options: A) Stock currently in the warehouse
B) Stock that has been ordered from suppliers but not yet delivered
C) Stock that is ready for shipment to customers
D) Stock that has been rejected due to quality issues
questions.answer: B) Stock that has been ordered from suppliers but not yet delivered
questions.explanation: Scheduled receipts are also known as the pipeline stock; that means, the company has placed order on to its suppliers and the suppliers has not yet delivered that stock; that means, that stock is in transit. It will be also known as the pipeline stock.

questions.question: The net requirement in MRP is calculated by subtracting the available stock at stores and scheduled receipts from what?
questions.answer: C) Planned requirement
questions.explanation: The net requirement is calculated based on the formula which is net requirement equals the planned requirement minus available stock at warehouse, that is available stock at stores plus the scheduled receipts from purchasing or production.

questions.question: What is a Bill of Material (BOM)?
options: A) A financial statement listing all assets and liabilities
B) A document detailing customer orders
C) A complete formally structured list which make up the components of a product or assembly
D) A report on production facility maintenance schedules
questions.answer: C) A complete formally structured list which make up the components of a product or assembly
questions.explanation: A bill of material is a complete formally structured list which make up the components of a product or assembly.

questions.question: How is the Bill of Materials typically stored in a computer database?
options: B) In the form of an inverted tree structure
D) As a relational table without hierarchy
questions.answer: B) In the form of an inverted tree structure
questions.explanation: In the computer database, the bill of materials is stored in the form of an inverted tree structure.

questions.question: Besides material identification number, quantity, and unit of measure, what other crucial information is indicated in the Bill of Material for each item?
options: C) Indicator for purchase or production
questions.answer: C) Indicator for purchase or production
questions.explanation: The bill of material is basically a list containing the material identification number of each item together with the quantity, the unit of measure and indicator for purchase or production.

questions.question: The process of "explosion of bill of materials" helps to calculate what?
options: A) The total sales revenue for a product
B) The planned requirement for an item
C) The cost of labor for production
D) The market demand for a product
questions.answer: B) The planned requirement for an item
questions.explanation: Plan requirement is then calculated through explosion of bill of materials. The exploded requirements must be known to compute the plan requirement for that item.

questions.question: After a production department has created products based on a production order, what is the next step in the simplified manufacturing process?
options: A) The customer places a new order
B) The warehouse issues a planned order
C) The production order is updated, and products are shipped to the warehouse
D) A material withdrawal slip is generated
questions.answer: C) The production order is updated, and products are shipped to the warehouse
questions.explanation: After production department has created the products based on this production order, it updates the production order specifying that as planned, a specific number of units of product can now be shipped to the warehouse and that is stocked in the warehouse.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT explicitly mentioned as a manufacturing activity?
questions.answer: D) Customer relationship management
questions.explanation: Manufacturing activities basically deal with planning, development and maintenance of production facilities. Customer relationship management is not listed.

questions.question: A "pull process" in manufacturing is characterized by:
options: A) Production based on anticipated customer demand
B) Production generated by a specific customer order
C) Building up inventory in anticipation of sales
D) Minimizing the need for production orders
questions.answer: B) Production generated by a specific customer order
questions.explanation: Make-to-order process is basically known as pull process, as if the customer is pulling the product from the assembly line or from the factory on to them. So, here production takes place based on confirmed order from the customer.

questions.question: When a planned order reaches the production department, who authorizes the order and issues a production order?
questions.answer: C) The production controller
questions.explanation: Once this planned order reaches the production department, the production controller authorizes the order and issues a production order.

questions.question: The primary objective of any information system supporting the production management function is to:
options: A) Reduce the number of employees
B) Provide all information required for optimal production of goods and services
questions.answer: B) Provide all information required for optimal production of goods and services
questions.explanation: The primary objective of any information systems that supports this production management function or manufacturing management function is to basically provide all those information which will be required for optimal production of goods and services.

questions.question: Which of the following is an example of strategic information for manufacturing management?
questions.answer: C) Policies on machine replacement
questions.explanation: Policies on machine replacement, augmentation of resources, modernization of equipment are examples of strategic information.

questions.question: Computing or reporting on the performance measures of machines depending on breakdown histories and cost of repair and failure is an example of what type of information?
questions.answer: C) Tactical
questions.explanation: Tactical information comprises of computing or reporting on the performance measures of machines depending on the breakdown histories and cost of repair and failure.

questions.question: Determining preventive maintenance schedules of machines is an example of what type of information required for manufacturing management?
questions.answer: C) Operational
questions.explanation: Determining preventive maintenance schedules of machines; all these are examples of operational information which is required for effectively performing the manufacturing management function.

questions.question: The production planning subsystem maintains data on orders for:
questions.answer: B) Repetitive manufacturing
questions.explanation: Production planning subsystem maintains data on orders for repetitive manufacturing, costs of production data and so on.

questions.question: “Routing” in the context of the production planning subsystem refers to:
options: A) The process of delivering finished goods to customers
B) The path a product follows to be converted from raw materials to finished goods, including machines and sequence
C) The financial accounting process for production costs
D) The method for acquiring new raw materials
questions.answer: B) The path a product follows to be converted from raw materials to finished goods, including machines and sequence
questions.explanation: Routing means all those that the route that the product will follow in order to get converted from the raw materials to the finished good stage; that means, through which machines and in what sequence the product will flow.

questions.question: While MRP focuses on integrating production, purchasing, and inventory management of interdependent items, what does the "explosion of bill of materials" primarily help to determine?
options: A) The final selling price of a product
B) The total quantity of each item required to meet the planned requirement of the finished product
D) The marketing strategy for a new product
questions.answer: B) The total quantity of each item required to meet the planned requirement of the finished product
questions.explanation: We can explode a bill of material to show the total quantity of each item which will be required to meet the planned requirement of the finished product.

questions.question: If the planned requirement for an item is 500 units, available stock at stores is 100 units, and scheduled receipts are 50 units, what is the net requirement (excluding safety stock)?
questions.answer: C) 350 units
questions.explanation: Net requirement = Planned Requirement - (Available Stock + Scheduled Receipts) = 500 - (100 + 50) = 500 - 150 = 350 units.

questions.question: A key piece of information included in a Bill of Material for each item is whether it will be:
options: B) Purchased from an outside vendor or made in-house
C) Designed by engineers or outsourced
D) Stored in a cold or dry environment
questions.answer: B) Purchased from an outside vendor or made in-house
questions.explanation: The bill of material indicates whether the item will be manufactured in house or procured from some outside vendor.

questions.question: What document is issued by the warehouse as soon as it receives finished goods from production?
questions.answer: C) Goods receipts document
questions.explanation: As soon as the warehouse receives the finished goods, it issues a goods receipts document that certifies how many units of a product it has received.

questions.question: In a make-to-stock (push process) strategy, if customers do not buy the products, what cost does the company have to bear?
options: B) Cost of holding finished goods inventory
C) Cost of raw material acquisition
D) Cost of production facility maintenance
questions.answer: B) Cost of holding finished goods inventory
questions.explanation: If customers really do not buy those products, then these products will remain as finished good stock and company will have to bear the cost of holding that finished goods inventory.

questions.question: If the net requirement formula is adjusted to include safety stock, how does it change?
options: A) Net requirement = Planned Requirement + Available Stock + Scheduled Receipts + Safety Stock
B) Net requirement = Planned Requirement - Available Stock - Scheduled Receipts - Safety Stock
C) Net requirement = Planned Requirement - Available Stock - Scheduled Receipts + Safety Stock
D) Net requirement = Planned Requirement + Safety Stock
questions.answer: C) Net requirement = Planned Requirement - Available Stock - Scheduled Receipts + Safety Stock
questions.explanation: In computing the net requirement, if we also take into consideration the safety stock, then the net requirement will be the plan requirement minus available stock at stores minus pipeline stock plus the safety stock which is required.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a function typically supported by the production planning subsystem?
questions.answer: C) Managing customer complaints
questions.explanation: The production planning subsystem generates sales forecasts and plans, maintains the bill of material, and supports routing, scheduling, and loading. Managing customer complaints is not listed as its function.

questions.question: Manufacturing activities include the acquisition and storage of materials needed for:
questions.answer: B) Production
questions.explanation: Manufacturing activities basically deal with... acquisition and storage of materials needed for production.

questions.question: A material withdrawal slip is generated by the production department to acquire materials needed for:
options: B) Starting the production of a specific product
questions.answer: B) Starting the production of a specific product
questions.explanation: To assemble a finished product production department will generate a material withdrawal slip which will list all of the needed parts and then this document will be forwarded to the stores or the warehouse. This happens after a production order is issued to start production.

questions.question: Which type of information system would typically support the identification of critical bottlenecks in production and alternate production schedules based on resource availability?
questions.answer: C) Tactical Information System
questions.explanation: Identification of critical bottlenecks in production, identification of alternate production schedules based on availability of tools, machines, materials and personnel are examples of tactical information required for a manufacturing function, supported by information systems for manufacturing management.

questions.question: Production planning has evolved from which concept?
questions.answer: C) Materials Requirement Planning (MRP)
questions.explanation: Production planning has evolved from materials requirement planning which in short commonly known as MRP.

questions.question: A production order is described as a written authorization to:
options: B) Start the production of a certain amount of specific product
questions.answer: B) Start the production of a certain amount of specific product
questions.explanation: The production controller authorizes the order and issues a production order which is a written authorization to start the production of a certain amount of specific product.

questions.question: The concept of "holding finished goods inventory" is most relevant to which manufacturing strategy?
questions.answer: C) Make-to-stock
questions.explanation: Make-to-stock production process occurs when a company produces goods to create or increase an inventory that is finished goods which are stored in the warehouse and are available for sales. The company bears the cost of holding this inventory if not sold.

questions.question: If parts listed on a material withdrawal slip are not available in the stores or warehouse, what is the next course of action for the company?
options: B) Procure them through the procurement process
C) Wait for new customer orders
D) Issue a goods receipts document
questions.answer: B) Procure them through the procurement process
questions.explanation: If the parts are not available then the company have to procure them, they have to purchase them through the procurement process.

questions.question: The goal of an information system for manufacturing management is to provide information for optimally deploying resources to maximize production, preferably at the:
questions.answer: B) Least cost
questions.explanation: The goal of production or manufacturing management is to optimally deploy human resources, machines and materials to maximize production of goods and services by the organization, preferably at the least cost.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT explicitly mentioned as a component of a Bill of Material entry?
questions.answer: D) Supplier's profit margin
questions.explanation: The bill of material is basically a list containing the material identification number of each item together with the quantity, the unit of measure and indicator for purchase or production. Supplier's profit margin is not mentioned.

questions.question: In the net requirement calculation, "scheduled receipts" are also referred to as:
questions.answer: C) Pipeline stock
questions.explanation: See the scheduled receipts are also known as the pipeline stock; that means, the company has placed order on to its suppliers and the suppliers has not yet delivered that stock; that means, that stock is in transit. It will be also known as the pipeline stock.

questions.question: A decision to acquire or merge with another manufacturing unit would require what type of information?
questions.answer: C) Strategic
questions.explanation: Introduction of new production technologies, acquisition and mergers of different units or companies are examples of strategic information.

questions.question: Ensuring quality at each step in production and controlling the action of machines and equipment on a daily basis are functions supported by:
questions.answer: C) Operational information
questions.explanation: Ensuring quality at each step in production, controlling the action of machines and equipment on a daily basis are examples of operational information.

questions.question: The production planning subsystem is described as a high-level module for managing the production function, including activities such as:
questions.answer: C) Routing, scheduling, and loading
questions.explanation: It is a high level module for managing the production function including activities such as routing, scheduling and loading.

questions.question: The planning process that integrates production, purchasing, and inventory management specifically focuses on which type of items?
questions.answer: C) Interdependent items
questions.explanation: The planning process that integrates production, purchasing and inventory management of interdependent items is the primary focus of materials requirement planning.

questions.question: Which of the following is an important function of manufacturing management that requires information systems support, following the determination of net material requirements?
questions.answer: B) Capacity planning
questions.explanation: After deciding on the net requirement for an item, the manufacturing manager needs to know if they have the requisite capacity, making capacity planning an important function supported by information systems for manufacturing management.

questions.question: What does 'capacity' primarily refer to in the context of manufacturing management?
options: A) The financial budget available for production
B) The ability to produce output per time period
C) The number of employees in a work center
D) The total inventory stored in a warehouse
questions.answer: B) The ability to produce output per time period
questions.explanation: Capacity basically refers to the ability to produce output per time period.

questions.question: Capacity requirements specify how much capacity is needed for what?
options: B) Individual orders at a specific time
questions.answer: B) Individual orders at a specific time
questions.explanation: Capacity requirements specify how much capacity is required for individual orders at a specific time.

questions.question: What is the purpose of capacity leveling?
options: A) To reduce the quality of products
B) To balance the requirement with the availability of capacity
C) To increase the cost of production
D) To eliminate the need for scheduling
questions.answer: B) To balance the requirement with the availability of capacity
questions.explanation: Capacity leveling means balancing the requirement with the availability, for example, by hiring extra capacity, buying machines, or outsourcing.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT explicitly mentioned as an activity supported by the production control function?
questions.answer: D) Employee recruitment
questions.explanation: The production control function helps maintain quality by keeping a close eye on activities such as ordering, follow-up on those orders, and inventory control. Employee recruitment is not mentioned.

questions.question: Manufacturing management information systems also provide support for which function that deals with activities giving shape to a product?
questions.answer: B) Product design
questions.explanation: Manufacturing management information systems also provide support for product design. The product design function deals with all the activities that give shape to a particular product.

questions.question: What does the Computer-Aided Design (CAD) subsystem primarily automate?
options: C) The creation and revision of product designs
questions.answer: C) The creation and revision of product designs
questions.explanation: The computer aided design subsystem basically automates the creation and revision of product designs using computers and sophisticated graphics software.

questions.question: A key advantage of CAD systems over traditional physical design methodology is that designers need to make a physical prototype only at what stage?
options: A) At the very beginning of the design process
B) Towards the end of the design process
C) For every minor design modification
D) Never, as CAD eliminates physical prototypes entirely
questions.answer: B) Towards the end of the design process
questions.explanation: Using a CAD workstation the designer need only make a physical prototype towards the end of the design process, because the design can be easily tested and changed on the computer.

questions.question: How do CAD systems contribute to the 'time to market' for new products?
options: A) They increase the time to market due to complexity.
B) They have no impact on the time to market.
C) They minimize the time to market by saving time and cost.
D) They only affect the cost, not the time.
questions.answer: C) They minimize the time to market by saving time and cost.
questions.explanation: CAD systems save time and cost; as a result, the time to market for a new product or a new variant is minimized.

questions.question: Which companies were mentioned as benefiting from CAD systems for engine cylinder design and other applications?
options: B) Ford Motor Company, Tata Motors, and Jaguar Land Rover
questions.answer: B) Ford Motor Company, Tata Motors, and Jaguar Land Rover
questions.explanation: Ford Motor Company used a computer simulation through this CAD system to create an engine cylinder. Similarly, CAD systems have also provided many benefits to companies like Tata Motors as well as Jaguar Land Rover.

questions.question: CAD software's ability to provide design specifications for tooling and manufacturing processes results in what?
options: B) Increased time and money expenditure
C) Significant savings in time and money with fewer manufacturing problems
D) A complete elimination of manufacturing processes
questions.answer: C) Significant savings in time and money with fewer manufacturing problems
questions.explanation: This ability of CAD software to provide design specifications for the tooling and manufacturing processes saves a great deal of time and money, while producing a manufacturing process with far fewer problems.

questions.question: CAD systems also supply data for what manufacturing process, also known as additive manufacturing?
questions.answer: C) Three-dimensional (3D) printing
questions.explanation: Computer aided design systems basically also supply data for three dimensional printing 3D printing. In manufacturing management this is also known as additive manufacturing.

questions.question: Additive manufacturing uses machines to make solid objects in what manner?
options: A) By removing material from a block
B) By molding liquid into a shape
C) Layer by layer from specifications to a digital file
D) Through a single, continuous extrusion process
questions.answer: C) Layer by layer from specifications to a digital file
questions.explanation: Additive manufacturing uses machines to make solid objects layer by layer from specifications to a digital file.

questions.question: For what applications is additive manufacturing currently being used?
options: A) Mass production of standard consumer goods
B) Producing prototypes and customized manufacturing work
questions.answer: B) Producing prototypes and customized manufacturing work
questions.explanation: Additive manufacturing is currently being used for producing prototypes and customized manufacturing work.

questions.question: What kind of subsystem is known for having visualization, rendering, and simulation capabilities that go far beyond conventional CAD systems?
questions.answer: C) Virtual Reality (VR) systems
questions.explanation: Virtual reality systems have visualization, rendering and simulation capabilities that go far beyond the capabilities provided by conventional CAD systems.

questions.question: In many virtual reality systems, what does the user often wear to enhance the immersive experience?
options: B) Special clothing, headgear, and equipment
C) Only a simple pair of headphones
D) A lab coat and safety glasses
questions.answer: B) Special clothing, headgear, and equipment
questions.explanation: In many virtual reality systems, the user wears special clothing, headgear and equipment depending on the application that they are visualizing.

questions.question: What is the function of sensors embedded in the special clothing worn by users in VR systems?
options: A) To provide haptic feedback only
B) To record every movement of the users and transmit information back to the computer
C) To generate audio cues for the user
D) To project images onto the clothing
questions.answer: B) To record every movement of the users and transmit information back to the computer
questions.explanation: Those special clothing which are being worn by the user contains sensors, that record every movement of the users and not only it records but also immediately transmits that information back to the computer.

questions.question: For a virtual reality simulation of a house, what might a user need in addition to special clothing?
options: B) Special type of goggles containing video screens, audio attachments, and feeling gloves
C) A physical model of the house
questions.answer: B) Special type of goggles containing video screens, audio attachments, and feeling gloves
questions.explanation: The user may also need special type of goggles containing video screens and sometimes those goggles might also contain some audio attachments and feeling gloves. So, that the user can get grossly immersed in the computer feedback.

questions.question: In a highly dynamic business environment with complex production processes, what is the characteristic of the data required?
options: A) It is minimal and easily managed manually.
B) It is massive in volume and complex.
C) It is static and rarely changes.
D) It is only relevant for financial departments.
questions.answer: B) It is massive in volume and complex.
questions.explanation: In a highly dynamic business environment with complex production processes, volumes of data which are required are massive.

questions.question: What is the role of a manufacturing management system regarding complex data?
options: B) To store, manage, and process huge volumes of complex data to guide managers
C) To manually sort all data
D) To only collect data, not process it
questions.answer: B) To store, manage, and process huge volumes of complex data to guide managers
questions.explanation: Manufacturing management system stores and manages this huge volume of complex data, it processes that data and guides the managers in achieving effective control of production activities.

questions.question: Which system, also known as a stock control system, is mentioned as a part of the manufacturing management information system that helps manage inventory automatically?
questions.answer: C) Inventory Control System
questions.explanation: As for example, the inventory control system which is also known as stock control system is a part of manufacturing management information system and this makes it easy to manage inventory automatically.

questions.question: In modern enterprise resource planning (ERP) systems like SAP or Oracle, how are information systems for different functions typically structured?
options: A) They are used in isolated manners.
B) They are completely separate and do not interact.
D) They are replaced by manual processes.
questions.answer: C) They are integrated together.
questions.explanation: If you look at enterprise planning systems resource planning systems like SAP or oracle you will find that, this kind of MIS which was previously used in isolated manners no longer exists. All this different functions information systems to support functions like say manufacturing management, materials management, finance and costing, quality maintenance function everything is integrated together.

questions.question: Why is it still important to discuss information systems for separate functions, even though they are integrated in modern ERPs?
options: A) Because integration is a temporary trend.
B) To understand the facilities, advantages, and primary features of how these integrated systems support each function.
C) Because isolated systems are more efficient.
D) To discourage the use of integrated systems.
questions.answer: B) To understand the facilities, advantages, and primary features of how these integrated systems support each function.
questions.explanation: But we are discussing the information systems for this separate function because even though we integrate, we must get to know that what are the facilities and advantages and primary features of those integrated systems are; how those integrated systems support each and every function.

questions.question: What is the primary goal of information systems for manufacturing management?
options: A) To replace human managers entirely.
B) To support the production management or manufacturing management function.
C) To only handle financial transactions.
questions.answer: B) To support the production management or manufacturing management function.
questions.explanation: We will continue on with the concepts of information systems which are used for supporting the production management or manufacturing management function.

questions.question: What is capacity requirement planning (CRP) described as?
options: A) A tool for financial forecasting.
B) A tool for determining available capacity, capacity requirements, and carrying out capacity leveling.
C) A method for marketing new products.
D) A system for managing human resources.
questions.answer: B) A tool for determining available capacity, capacity requirements, and carrying out capacity leveling.
questions.explanation: Capacity requirement planning is basically a tool for determining available capacity and capacity requirements and for carrying out capacity leveling.

questions.question: If a company does not have the requisite capacity for production, what options are mentioned for capacity leveling?
options: A) Reducing product quality or stopping production.
B) Hiring extra capacity, buying new machines, or outsourcing requirements.
C) Increasing prices to reduce demand.
D) Relying solely on existing resources without adjustment.
questions.answer: B) Hiring extra capacity, buying new machines, or outsourcing requirements.
questions.explanation: Whether we will hire some extra capacity we will buy some extra machines or we will outsource some of these requirements to some external supplier.

questions.question: What information is needed for scheduling production to maintain uniformity, as part of capacity leveling?
options: B) Information generated from the manufacturing management information system.
C) Information about global economic trends.
questions.answer: B) Information generated from the manufacturing management information system.
questions.explanation: Also capacity leveling means how do I schedule my production such that I maintain an uniformity in doing that the scheduling will require some information. Now that information is generated from the manufacturing management information system.

questions.question: The production control operation helps maintain product quality by keeping a close eye on which activities?
options: B) Ordering, follow-up on orders, and inventory control.
C) Research and development of new technologies.
D) Legal compliance and regulatory affairs.
questions.answer: B) Ordering, follow-up on orders, and inventory control.
questions.explanation: This production control function helps maintain quality of the products by keeping a close eye on activities such as ordering, follow up on those order and inventory control.

questions.question: What is the main purpose of the product design function?
options: B) To deal with all activities that give shape to a particular product.
C) To oversee the distribution of finished goods.
questions.answer: B) To deal with all activities that give shape to a particular product.
questions.explanation: The production product design function deals with all the activities that give shape to a particular product.

questions.question: What kind of software is used by the CAD subsystem for creating and revising product designs?
questions.answer: B) Sophisticated graphics software
questions.explanation: The computer aided design subsystem basically automates the creation and revision of product designs using computers and sophisticated graphics software.

questions.question: Why is new product design or modification of existing products considered an important input for the manufacturing management function?
options: A) It is irrelevant to manufacturing.
B) It requires information support for which production information systems are used.
D) It is a purely manual process.
questions.answer: B) It requires information support for which production information systems are used.
questions.explanation: New product design or modification of existing products is an important input for the manufacturing management function for which information support is required and this is being provided by this production information systems or manufacturing information system.

questions.question: In traditional physical design methodology, what process is often repeated multiple times, leading to high costs and time consumption?
options: B) Making a mould, testing a prototype physically, and iterating.
C) Financial auditing of design expenses.
questions.answer: B) Making a mould, testing a prototype physically, and iterating.
questions.explanation: Each new product design or design modification requires a mould to be made and a prototype to be tested physically. If this process is repeated many times, a lot of expenses will be incurred and a lot of time will be consumed.
